title: Vision Transformer-Conditioned UNet for Domain-Adaptive Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: A full UNet with local inductive bias and full-res decoding is conditioned on frozen pretrained ViT representations through learnable tokens and a two-way attention decoder, aimed at sparse, fine, low-SNR targets.
adaptation: Keep the house U-Net++/ResNet-34 detail path; add cross-attention from its bottleneck and decoder nodes to frozen DINOv3 ViT-L tokens of the same cell. The ViT supplies context for half-cut layout and scuff streaks (E1); 1-2 px localisation stays with the CNN. PF schedule for the CNN.
min_experiment: Arm: house PF + ViT-L token conditioning; baseline: house PF; 5-fold module-grouped CV crack IoU and inactive IoU, then E1 crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU. Kill if E1 crack relF1@2 < +0.03 or CV crack IoU drops > 0.012.
evidence: R: abstract reports gains over baselines on MRI and CT semantic segmentation with frozen ViT; no numbers retrieved, no thin-line data.
prior_overlap: none; no ViT-conditioned CNN run exists.

alt_notes.adaptation: Keep the house U-Net++ / ResNet-34 as the pixel path for 1 to 2 px localisation; add cross-attention from its bottleneck and decoder stages to frozen DINOv3 ViT-L tokens of the same cell so half-cut layout and scuff context come from the ViT. About 200 lines of our own code (official code not released).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house PF + frozen DINOv3 ViT-L conditioning; baseline house PF; 5-fold CV crack IoU / relF1@2 / inactive IoU, then E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU. Kill: E1 crack relF1@2 gain < +0.03 or CV crack IoU drop > 0.012. About 20 GPU-h.
